group.passage:
It used to be thought that journalists were relatively safe from the threat of job loss due to automation. [[1]] But as artificial intelligence (AI) developed, writing programs became increasingly capable of performing journalistic tasks. For example, they can produce readable articles twenty-four hours a day, which was impossible in the past.
The threat to journalists’ jobs, then, is obvious. After all, why employ a team of journalists when an AI program can report the news faster and at a much larger scale for free? [[2]] The British Broadcasting Company (BBC), for example, cut 70 jobs from its news department after introducing AI writing programs in 2020, leading many to wonder if their job could be the next.
However, not all journalists fear the introduction of AI. [[3]] Imagine those time-consuming tasks all being done by AI. This would allow journalists to focus on more sophisticated and complex forms of journalism, such as opinion pieces and investigative reporting. [[4]] All in all, if journalists can use AI properly, it has the potential to enrich the field rather than degrade it.

options_bank.A: Instead, some even see AI as a blessing since it is best suited to heavy articles with simple facts and figures, such as financial reports.
options_bank.B: Indeed, some journalists have already fallen victim to this profit-driven logic.
options_bank.C: These types of writing are impossible for AI to replicate, at least for now.
options_bank.D: After all, while machines can easily outperform humans in many tasks, producing a well-written article requires a special kind of intelligence.

tags.topic: AI writing programs and the future of journalism
